SuSiEOut: fine-mapping when causal variants may be omitted

Source: R/SuSiEOut-package.R
SuSiEOut-package.Rd

SuSiEOut implements SuSiE-OUT, a summary-statistic fine-mapping model for loci at which a causal variant may have been removed from the tested set, for example by a minor allele frequency (MAF) threshold or a SNP-only filter. Each sparse effect can be null, assigned to a tested variant, or assigned to an omitted variant (an OUT state). An omitted variant is represented by its LD fingerprint: its correlations with the tested variants, measured in a sequencing reference panel that contains it.

Main functions

  • susieout_fit() fits the model at one locus.

  • susieout_fit_grid() and susieout_fit_nuisance_grid() average fits over polygenic and LD-mismatch settings.

  • susieout_candidate_support() and susieout_credible_sets() summarize a fit.

  • susieout_simulate_locus() generates loci with known causal variants.

Naming

Arguments and fields named examined_* refer to tested variants; excluded_* and outside_* refer to omitted variants.

Acknowledgements

SuSiE-OUT builds directly on the Sum of Single Effects (SuSiE) model of Wang, Sarkar, Carbonetto and Stephens (2020) and its summary-statistic extension SuSiE-RSS (Zou, Carbonetto, Wang and Stephens, 2022), and it reuses susieR as a reference implementation. We are grateful to the SuSiE authors for making their methods and software openly available. SuSiEOut is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the SuSiE authors or the susieR maintainers.

References

Wang G, Sarkar A, Carbonetto P, Stephens M (2020). A simple new approach to variable selection in regression, with application to genetic fine mapping. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B 82, 1273–1300. doi:10.1111/rssb.12388

Zou Y, Carbonetto P, Wang G, Stephens M (2022). Fine-mapping from summary data with the "Sum of Single Effects" model. PLOS Genetics 18, e1010299. doi:10.1371/journal.pgen.1010299
